Tracks container for circular trajectories

Source: R/Tracks.R
Tracks-class.Rd

Tracks container for circular trajectories

Construct a Tracks

Usage

tracks(
  df,
  id = "id",
  time = "time",
  angle = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  rel_x = NULL,
  rel_y = NULL,
  angle_unit = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  normalize_xy = FALSE,
  origin = NULL,
  radius = NULL,
  meta = list(),
  transform_history = NULL
)

# S4 method for class 'Tracks'
length(x)

# S4 method for class 'Tracks,ANY,missing,missing'
x[i]

# S4 method for class 'Tracks'
c(x, ..., recursive = FALSE)

Arguments

df

data.frame in long form

id, time

Columns naming trajectory id and time

angle

Optional angle column (radians or degrees, see angle_unit)

x, y

Optional cartesian columns; if provided, converted to unit circle and angle inferred

rel_x, rel_y

Optional column names for pre-transformed relative coordinates (centred on the origin, unit-circle scaled). Both must be supplied together or not at all.

angle_unit

Units of provided angle ("radians" or "degrees"); stored internally as radians

weight

Optional weight column name; weights must be finite and >= 0

normalize_xy

If FALSE (default), (x,y) are kept as supplied. If TRUE, each trajectory is independently centred on its own bounding-box midpoint and scaled so its furthest point sits at radius 1. This is a shape-preserving transform ONLY: because each trajectory is translated by a different amount, it does NOT preserve bearing relative to a fixed arena origin, and must not be used as a substitute for metric calibration. Raw coordinates are retained in `<x>_raw`/`<y>_raw` when enabled. Prefer pre-calibrated input, or the landmark-relative frame (`rel_x`/`rel_y`, see `coords = "relative"` in [derive_headings()]) when a per-trial reference direction is available.

origin

Optional length-2 numeric `c(x, y)` giving a fixed unit-circle centre in the raw coordinate units. Supplied together with `radius`, it calibrates every trajectory uniformly via `(xy - origin) / radius`, a similarity that preserves bearings measured from the origin (unlike `normalize_xy`, which centres each trajectory on its own bounding box). Mutually exclusive with `normalize_xy = TRUE`. Raw coordinates are retained in `<x>_raw`/`<y>_raw`. For example, in an experimental arena `origin` is the arena centre and `radius` its edge distance in pixels.

radius

Optional positive finite scalar: the raw distance mapping to `rho = 1`. Required together with `origin`.

meta

Free-form list of metadata

transform_history

Optional tibble describing transformation steps applied to the trajectories. Must contain columns `step`, `order`, `id`, `implementation`, `params`, and `depends_on`.

i

Trajectory identifiers (character ids, numeric indices, or logical vector)

...

Additional Tracks objects to append. All inputs must share identical column mapping and angle unit, have no colliding trajectory ids, and agree on frame_rate/time_unit/distance_scale/distance_unit/normalize_xy metadata (including all-unset); mismatches error rather than silently picking one input's values. Per-id metadata (e.g. `reference`) and the attrition records of the loads are merged across all inputs. A subset carries the whole record of its load, so recombining subsets of one load repeats that record.

recursive

Ignored; maintained for signature compatibility

Value

A Tracks S4 object

Slots

data

data.frame of trajectory observations in long form

cols

list mapping required column names (id/time/angle/optional x,y,weight)

angle_unit

character describing the original angle unit supplied

meta

list of additional metadata attached to the set

Invariants

Every Tracks satisfies the following. They are checked when the object is built and whenever methods::validObject() runs, which the package's own transforms do (a direct slot write is not checked until then):

  • ids are never missing, and the rows of each id are contiguous;

  • time is finite and strictly increasing within each id, so no time is repeated within a trajectory;

  • angles are finite and lie in [0, 2*pi);

  • coordinates are finite: x/y, and the relative and raw pairs where those columns are stored;

  • weights, when a weight column is named, are finite and >= 0 (a zero weight excludes an observation).

A Tracks therefore never holds a missing detection: remove those before construction (see on_invalid in read_tracks).

tracks() reports violations as an error of class radiatR_invalid_tracks. Its problems field is a data frame with one row per rule, column and row: rule, column, row (the row of the data frame supplied) and id; rows and ids give the union. When called through read_tracks, rows are those of the combined table passed to tracks() (after any rows removed by on_invalid = "drop"), not line numbers in a file.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  id   = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 3),
  time = rep(1:3, 2),
  x    = c(0, 0.3, 0.6, 0, -0.2, -0.5),
  y    = c(0, 0.2, 0.5, 0, 0.3, 0.7)
)
ts <- tracks(df, x = "x", y = "y")
ts
#> Tracks: 2 trajectories, 6 observations
#> Columns: id='id', time='time', angle='angle' (radians), x='x', y='y'
#>   id time    x   y     angle
#> 1  a    1  0.0 0.0 0.0000000
#> 2  a    2  0.3 0.2 0.5880026
#> 3  a    3  0.6 0.5 0.6947383
#> 4  b    1  0.0 0.0 0.0000000
#> 5  b    2 -0.2 0.3 2.1587989
#> 6  b    3 -0.5 0.7 2.1910458
length(ts)
#> [1] 2
ts["b"]
#> Tracks: 1 trajectories, 3 observations
#> Columns: id='id', time='time', angle='angle' (radians), x='x', y='y'
#>   id time    x   y    angle
#> 4  b    1  0.0 0.0 0.000000
#> 5  b    2 -0.2 0.3 2.158799
#> 6  b    3 -0.5 0.7 2.191046

# combine objects with the same column mapping
more <- tracks(data.frame(id = "c", time = 1:2, x = c(0, 0.4), y = c(0, -0.4)),
               x = "x", y = "y")
length(c(ts, more))
#> [1] 3

# pixel coordinates: arena centre (320, 240), edge 200 px from it
px <- data.frame(id = "d", time = 1:3,
                 x = c(320, 380, 450), y = c(240, 280, 330))
tracks(px, x = "x", y = "y", origin = c(320, 240), radius = 200)
#> Tracks: 1 trajectories, 3 observations
#> Columns: id='id', time='time', angle='angle' (radians), x='x', y='y', raw_x='x_raw', raw_y='y_raw'
#> Transform steps: calibrate_unit_circle 
#>   id time    x    y x_raw y_raw     angle
#> 1  d    1 0.00 0.00   320   240 0.0000000
#> 2  d    2 0.30 0.20   380   280 0.5880026
#> 3  d    3 0.65 0.45   450   330 0.6055447
